title: Helsing backer Plural raises $1.1B to fund Europe’s next moonshots
slides: Can Europe's next Helsing come from this $1.1B bet?
Plural's new fund targets deep tech moonshots
But most of the capital goes to founders only now
Later-stage European startups face a funding cliff
Ask your team: which moonshot dies without this check?
thread_text:
1. Europe's $1.1B moonshot

Plural's new fund is betting big on deep tech, but most of the capital now goes to founders only. That leaves later-stage startups staring at a funding cliff.

2. The founder-only shift

Investors are pouring money into early-stage founders, but later-stage European startups are struggling to raise follow-on rounds. The gap is widening.

3. Funding cliff ahead

Later-stage European startups face a funding cliff as capital concentrates on early bets. Without follow-on, even promising moonshots could die.

4. Can Helsing 2.0 emerge?

With $1.1B aimed at deep tech, Europe hopes for its next Helsing. But the founder-only focus may starve the very companies that need scale-up capital.

5. Which moonshot dies?

Ask your team: which moonshot dies without this check? If you can't name one, you're not paying attention to the funding cliff.

instagram.caption:
One billion dollars just landed on European deep tech, but almost none of it reaches companies that already shipped a product.

Plural, the backer behind Helsing, closed a $1.1B fund aimed at moonshots. Most of the money is earmarked for founders only, at the earliest stage.

Later-stage startups are left staring at a funding cliff. Without follow-on rounds, promising companies stall before they scale.

If you're building in Europe, your next round just got harder to find.
